source_text: »Οἴνῳ δὲ ὀλίγῳ χρῶ«, τῷ Τιμοθέῳ ὑδροποτοῦντι, »διὰ τὸν στόμαχόν σου«, φησὶν ὁ ἀπόστολος, παγκάλως νοσηλευομένῳ καὶ πλαδῶντι σώματι κατάλληλον τὸ ἐπιστῦφον βοήθημα προσφέρων, ὀλίγον δὲ ἐγκρίνων τοῦτο, μὴ λάθῃ τὸ βοήθημα διὰ πλῆθος ἄλλης θεραπείας δεόμενον. φυσικὸν μὲν οὖν καὶ νηφάλιον ποτὸν ἀναγκαῖον διψῶσίν ἐστιν ὕδωρ. τοῦτο ἐκ τῆς ἀκροτόμου πέτρας κατειβόμενον τοῖς παλαιοῖς τῶν Ἑβραίων μονότροπον σωφροσύνης ὁ κύριος ἐχορήγει ποτόν, νήφειν δὲ μάλιστα ἐχρῆν τοὺς ἔτι πλανωμένους. ἔπειτα ἡ ἄμπελος ἡ ἁγία τὸν βότρυν ἐβλάστησεν τὸν προφητικόν. τοῦτο σημεῖον τοῖς εἰς ἀνάπαυσιν ἐκ τῆς πλάνης πεπαιδαγωγημένοις, ὁ μέγας βότρυς, ὁ λόγος ὁ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν θλιβείς, τὸ αἷμα τῆς σταφυλῆς ὕδατι κίρνασθαι ἐθελήσαντος τοῦ λόγου, ὡς καὶ τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ σωτηρίᾳ κίρναται διττὸν δὲ τὸ αἷμα τοῦ κυρίου· τὸ μέν ἐστιν αὐτοῦ σαρκικόν, ᾧ τῆς φθορᾶς λελυτρώμεθα, τὸ δὲ πνευματικόν, τοῦτ᾿ ἔστιν ᾧ κεχρίσμεθα. καὶ τοῦτ᾿ ἔστι πιεῖν τὸ αἷμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, τῆς κυριακῆς μεταλαβεῖν ἀφθαρσίας· ἰσχὺς δὲ τοῦ λόγου τὸ πνεῦμα, ὡς αἷμα σαρκός. ἀναλόγως τοίνυν κίρναται ὁ μὲν οἶνος τῷ ὕδατι, τῷ δὲ ἀνθρώπῳ τὸ πνεῦμα, καὶ τὸ μὲν εἰς πίστιν εὐωχεῖ, τὸ κρᾶμα, τὸ δὲ εἰς ἀφθαρσίαν ὁδηγεῖ, τὸ πνεῦμα, ἡ δὲ ἀμφοῖν αὖθις κρᾶσις ποτοῦ τε καὶ λόγου εὐχαριστία κέκληται, χάρις ἐπαινουμένη καὶ καλή, ἧς οἱ κατὰ πίστιν μεταλαμβάνοντες ἁγιάζονται καὶ σῶμα καὶ ψυχήν, τὸ θεῖον κρᾶμα τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦ πατρικοῦ βουλήματος πνεύματι καὶ λόγῳ συγκιρνάντος μυστικῶς· καὶ γὰρ ὡς ἀληθῶς μὲν τὸ πνεῦμα ᾠκείωται τῇ ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ φερομένῃ ψυχῇ, ἡ δὲ σὰρξ τῷ λόγῳ, δι᾿ ἣν »ὁ λόγος γέγονεν σάρξ«. ἄγαμαι τοίνυν τοὺς αὐστηρὸν ἐπανῃρημένους βίον καὶ τῆς σωφροσύνης τὸ φάρμακον ἐπιποθοῦντας τὸ ὕδωρ, φεύγοντας δὲ ὅτι μάλιστα πορρωτάτω τὸν οἶνον οἷον πυρὸς ἀπειλήν. Ἀρέσκει οὖν τοὺς παῖδας καὶ τὰς κόρας ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πλεῖστον ἀπέχεσθαι τοῦ φαρμάκου τούτου· οὐ γὰρ κατάλληλον ζεούσῃ ἡλικίᾳ τῶν ὑγρῶν τὸ θερμότατον ἐπεγχεῖν, τὸν οἶνον, οἱονεὶ πῦρ ἐποχετεύοντας πυρί, ἐξ οὗ ὁρμαί τε ἄγριαι καὶ φλεγμαίνουσαι ἐπιθυμίαι καὶ διάπυρον ἦθος ἐκκαίεται προπετεῖς τε οἱ νέοι ἔνδοθεν χλιαινόμενοι ἐπὶ τὰς ὀρέξεις γίνονται, ὡς δὴ προὖπτον αὐτῶν τὴν βλάβην ἐλέγχεσθαι διὰ τοῦ σώματος, πεπαινομένων θᾶττον ἢ προσῆκεν τῶν τῆς ἐπιθυμίας μελῶν.
pass_a_gloss: The apostle says to Timothy, who drinks water, 'use a little wine' because of your stomach, offering suitable help to a body that is weak and sick, and he approves of a little of this, so that the help is not lost due to a large amount of other treatment. Water is a natural and sober drink that is necessary for those who are thirsty. The Lord provided water from the rock to the ancient Hebrews, a simple drink of sobriety, and it was especially necessary for those who were still wandering to be sober. Then the holy vine produced the prophetic cluster. This is a sign to those who have been instructed to rest from wandering, the great cluster, the Word who was pressed for us, the blood of the grape that the Word wished to be mixed with water, just as His own blood is mixed for salvation. The blood of the Lord is twofold: one is His fleshly blood, by which we are redeemed from corruption, and the other is spiritual, by which we are anointed. And this is to drink the blood of Jesus, to partake of the incorruption of the Lord. The power of the Word is the Spirit, just as blood is to flesh. Accordingly, wine is mixed with water, and the Spirit is mixed with man, and the mixture brings faith, and the Spirit leads to incorruption, and the mixture of both is called thanksgiving, a praised and good grace, by which those who partake in faith are sanctified in both body and soul, the divine mixture, with the Father's will, mixing man with Spirit and Word mysteriously. For the Spirit is truly joined to the soul that it carries, and the flesh is joined to the Word, through which 'the Word became flesh'. I praise those who have renounced a strict life and desire the water, the remedy of sobriety, and flee from wine as much as possible, as a threat of fire. It is pleasing to the children and the young women, for the most part, to abstain from this remedy, for it is not suitable to add the hottest thing, wine, to a youthful age that is already hot, as if pouring fire on fire, from which wild and inflamed desires and a fiery personality are kindled, and the young people, being inflamed within, become prone to desires, as if their damage is being reproved through their body, being corrupted more quickly than they should be, due to the members of desire.

pass_b_english: The apostle tells Timothy, who drinks only water, "Use a little wine" because of your stomach, offering a body that is weak and sick a suitable remedy, and he approves a small amount so that the remedy is not lost through needing too much other treatment (1 Timothy 5:23). Water is a natural and sober drink that is necessary for those who thirst. The Lord gave the ancient Hebrews water from the rock, a simple drink of sobriety, and it was especially necessary for those who were still wandering to be sober. Then the holy vine produced the prophetic cluster. This is a sign to those who have been instructed to rest from wandering: the great cluster, the Word who was pressed for us, wished His blood — the blood of the grape — to be mixed with water, just as His own blood is mixed for salvation. The blood of the Lord is twofold: one part is His fleshly blood, by which we are redeemed from corruption; the other is spiritual, by which we are anointed. And this is what it means to drink the blood of Jesus: to partake of the incorruption of the Lord. The power of the Word is the Spirit, just as blood is to flesh. Accordingly, wine is mixed with water, and the Spirit is mixed with humanity; the mixture brings faith, and the Spirit leads to incorruption. The mixture of both drink and Word is called thanksgiving, a praised and good grace, by which those who partake in faith are sanctified in both body and soul — the divine mixture, by which the Father's will mingles humanity with Spirit and Word mysteriously. For the Spirit is truly joined to the soul that it carries, and the flesh is joined to the Word, through which "the Word became flesh." I praise those who have renounced a strict life and desire the water, the remedy of sobriety, and who flee wine as far as possible, as a threat of fire. It is fitting that children and young women, for the most part, abstain from this remedy, for it is not suitable to add the hottest thing, wine, to a youthful age that is already hot, as if pouring fire on fire, from which wild and inflamed desires and a fiery character are kindled, and the young, being inflamed within, become prone to desires, as if their damage is reproved through their body, the members of desire being corrupted more quickly than they should.
